text:
Cheng: FYI ran the RoPE safety sweep today across Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen for long-context (>32k). Found an unexpected quality cliff on Mixtral when using the YARN variant beyond ~32k.
Maria: summary numbers?
Cheng: brief: Mixtral-YARN @64k: ppl +9% vs baseline; Mixtral-NTK @64k: ppl +2%; Llama-linear stable up to 48k. Perf: 2.8x token latency on Mixtral-YARN at 64k compared to NTK.
Sam: who changed kernel selector recently? sounds like a perf + quality combo issue.
Olga: I think the selector picked the fused attention kernel on those shapes which does a fallback path for headKV layout. That kernel does extra KV copies.
Cheng: yes trace shows repeated host->device memcpy around KV store ops during generation step 1..5. snippet from perf-bot trace:

```
perf-bot: trace 1767894321
--- op: build_kv_cache ---
copy: 3.1ms  size=64MB  direction=H2D
kv_write: 0.9ms
attn_fused: 12.4ms
copy: 3.0ms  size=64MB  direction=D2H
```

Maria: copy thrash explains latency. But why the ppl hit? KV layout + RoPE variant might change positional interpolation at extreme offsets.
Sam: could be numeric drift from float16 kernels + YARN scaling factors. Need cross-check with fp32 run.
Cheng: did fp32 run for a short subset — ppl regression persists but smaller: +4% instead of +9%. So numeric precision amplifies it.
Olga: hypothesis: kernel selects fused matmul path that applies rotary scaling in a way that assumes linear RoPE; with YARN/NTK we need a different elementwise op ordering. That could subtly alter attention weights at high positions.
Maria: can we force kernel selection to the 'kv-stream' path for Mixtral-YARN as a mitigation? If that avoids the fused path copies and uses our elementwise RoPE implementation it might fix ppl and perf.
Sam: patch idea: add a selector override heuristics: if model in {mixtral-*} and ropetype != linear and context_len > 32768 then prefer kernel=kv_stream and batch_threshold < X. quick flag: `--kernelselect=prefer_kv_stream`
Cheng: good. Also modify batching heuristic to avoid overly large batch accumulation for longctx single-stream (we saw batch builder waiting to fill 4 streams then flushing big combined KV writes). Set max_prefill_tokens=8k for longctx.
Olga: will run a 48h sweep with three dims: (kernel override ON/OFF) x (fp16/fp32) x (YARN/NTK/linear) and collect ppl + p50/p95 latency.
perf-bot: scheduling sweep job 1767894321-2 on cluster-gpu-a (est run 2h)
Maria: one more ask: log the headKV shape per step and an extra tag when we hit memcpy > 1ms to easily grep later.
Cheng: added tracing hook: `trace.kv_event(head_shape, memcpy_us)` in the branch.
Sam: thanks — if this fixes perf+quality we should also add a safety bound in model profiles: "max_rope_scale_length" per model variant to avoid auto-selecting YARN beyond safe range.
Olga: Agreed. I’ll collect safe bounds per model after the sweep and propose defaults (Mixtral: 48k, Qwen: 64k, Llama: 48k for head-kv layouts) — provisional.
Maria: perfect. Ping when the job finishes, especially if ppl delta > 5%.
perf-bot: job 1767894321-2 completed: artifacts -> s3://prod-perf/mixtral/1767894321/sweep.tar.gz (summary: Mixtral-YARN fp16 with kernelselect=kv_stream reduced ppl delta from +9% to +1.2% and median latency from 2.8x -> 1.05x)
Cheng: awesome, that confirms kernel path + precision both matter.
Sam: follow-ups: (1) land kernelselect flag behind an experiment, (2) add model profile safety bound, (3) adjust batcher for longctx. I’ll own (1).
Maria: I’ll draft the model-profile proposal for safety bounds.
Olga: I’ll upload the full traces and a small repro harness to /eng-runtime/benchmarks/rope-longctx.
Cheng: thanks team — good progress. :tada:
